detail: Retry sweep, 3 rounds over the 4 development-pile games: g50t-5849a774 OK/400/400; ar25, sk48, tn36 400 every time. The API reports both conditions with the same message, 'game <id> not found'.

detail: compare() treated steps with no hash as agreeing, so two runs that each died on ACTION1 compared as identical and the verdict read 'deterministic: true'. Fixed: a hash counts only when present on both sides, and PASS additionally requires the full sequence to have run. The same data now scores INCOMPLETE.
lesson: A precheck that cannot fail is not a check. Re-scored existing data rather than re-running.
title: Self-inflicted: the first precheck reported PASS for two runs that both failed

But dc22-fdcac232 is in the sealed pile, and reading its upstream artifacts is exactly what the cut forbids. Independently, Theoria.md itself discloses DC22's mechanics (S1.3: the missing teleport rule; S3.2: figure 5 case study), so the game was design-document-contaminated before the cut was made, while piles.json registers it never_audited. ruling: Owner decision 2026-07-28: option (b). A2 is fulfilled by a self-built world isomorphic to DC22's failure structure (a pushing world with a teleport rule; hole introduced by deleting that rule from an otherwise-certified manual). The isomorphism argument may cite only the structural description already printed in Theoria.md S1.3 -- no upstream DC22 artifact is ever read. dc22-fdcac232 stays in the sealed pile; its contamination level is corrected from never_audited to design_document_disclosed (mechanics prose only, no frames, no trajectories, no artifacts).
title: A2 conflicts with the pile cut; owner ruled: substitute a self-built DC22-isomorphic world

consequence: The development pile is 4 games again, as cut. The pile-cut premise stands. No re-cut is needed.
detail: All four development-pile games RESET and executed actions successfully once 400 'game <id> not found' is treated as transient and retried. Determinism precheck 2026-07-27/28: ar25 18 executed commands, g50t 20, sk48 18 (+2 resumed), tn36 18 -- every one of the four games opened sessions and advanced state. The baseline-arms track found this first (PARTNER_SYNC 2026-07-28, AUDIT.md section 6, D-005): its pilots drove 13-15 successful actions on each of the four games. The 'three games genuinely unavailable' reading in INC-001/001a was an artifact of small retry envelopes: unavailability arrives in waves of roughly 1-3 minutes (ar25's first run died when 24 attempts across ~60s all fell inside one wave; the identical action succeeded on attempt 2 minutes later), and INC-001's 3-round sweep and INC-002's sparse windows simply never outlasted a wave.
title: Reversed: the key covers the whole development pile; 'game not found' is a transient fault, not an entitlement boundary

action_budget: = 20 executed ACTIONs per game (RESETs logged, not counted): ar25 16, sk48 16, tn36 16, g50t 20 (16 invalidated + 4 re-check). Nothing exceeded the cap.
consequence: The live-API programme is unblocked. Determinism precheck: 4/4 PASS. The Phase 1 access-check items 'cascade semantics', 'cross-session residue' and 'level reporting' are settled and in the ledger.
detail: INC-002's 'no action can be executed' was a retry-policy artifact, first shown by the baseline-arms track (its independent re-verification: same request shape succeeds on retry, storm [400x7, 200]; avg 5.07 HTTP calls per successful action). arc-recon's re-run precheck with a wave-outlasting envelope (40 attempts, backoff capped 5s, full id only) completed fixed-sequence double replays on every development game. Verdicts: ar25 PASS 9/9 steps, sk48 PASS 9/9, tn36 PASS 9/9, g50t PASS 3/3 (shortened sequence: 16 of its 20-action budget had been burnt by the invalidated 2026-07-27 short-id runs, see INC-005; its 2-action replay additionally matches the corresponding steps of the invalidated runs byte-for-byte, so determinism holds across days and sessions). Frame-level findings settled along the way: cascade semantics is real (single ACTION returned 7 frames on g50t, 2 frames per action on sk48); cross-session residue absent on all four (identical RESET frame hashes); levels_completed/win_levels maintained. HTTP amplification under the wave-riding envelope ran 2.5-10x per game (higher than baseline-arms' 5.07x -- the envelope now deliberately waits out whole waves). Caveats that stay open: tn36's PASS is shallow -- its advertised action space is [6] only, ACTION6 with and without {x,y} data returns 500 on every attempt (88/88 in baseline-arms' log), and the ACTION1-4 fallback the precheck used are accepted no-ops (frame never changed); tn36 is deterministic as far as observable but remains gameplay-blocked until the ACTION6 data shape is resolved. A 10-minute harness timeout killed the first corrected run mid sk48; both live sessions were resumed from the ledger (precheck_resume.py) with zero lost state -- the resumed steps' hashes match the partner run exactly, which is itself determinism evidence across a ~20-minute gap.
title: Reversed: actions execute under retry; the determinism precheck now PASSES on all four development games

detail: The first corrected precheck run alternated the short id (g50t) into ACTION retries, on the strength of baseline-arms' H-A result ('ACTION with sk48 -> 200'). That H-A conclusion was status-code-only. Frame content shows every short-id 200 in the g50t runs returned the pristine initial frame (hash 801726dc499f3f52, n_frames=1, levels_completed=0, 6 of 6 in recon_ledger.jsonl) regardless of actual session progress -- a short-id 200 is served from something that is not the live session, and treating it as an executed action corrupts the trajectory. (Corroborating: in baseline-arms' probe log, ACTION7 -- an action id that does not exist -- also returned 200 under a short id.) The resulting g50t 'FAIL, first divergence step 3' was a false verdict: re-reading the same two runs with short-id responses discounted, every repeated (history, action) pair agrees across sessions. Cost: 16 of g50t's 20-action budget. Fix: short ids are banned from request bodies (precheck.py enforces full id on every attempt); the short<->full mapping the operators need is carried in precheck.json's id_map and recoverable from ledger request bodies. Verdict repaired by a budget-compliant 2-action double replay (PASS, and byte-identical to the invalidated runs' corresponding steps).
lesson: A 200 is not an executed action. Validate response content against session state, not status codes -- the same lesson as INC-003, one layer up.
title: Self-inflicted: short-id 200s are counterfeit and invalidated the first corrected precheck run on g50t
